content.title: About
content.content: Lamb (or mutton) loaf is a baked meat patty made from ground lamb or mutton, often mixed with onion, garlic, herbs, and sometimes breadcrumbs or rice. It has a rich aroma, mildly spiced flavor, and a dense yet tender texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lamb has a stronger, more distinctive flavor than beef due to higher levels of certain fatty acids.
Traditional lamb loaf recipes are popular in the Middle East, Mediterranean countries, and some regions of Russia.
Some versions include dried fruits (raisins, apricots) for a sweet‑savory contrast.
Lamb loaf is often served cold, sliced as an appetizer alongside wine or kefir drinks.
Cooking in a clay pot helps retain moisture and intensify the aroma.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Lamb provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich source of iron
items.content: The iron in lamb is highly bioavailable and supports healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Zinc
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Polyunsaturated fats
items.content: Lamb includes omega‑3 and omega‑6 fatty acids that are beneficial for heart health.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive consumption may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to lamb.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked ground meat can harbor pathogens; ensure internal temperature reaches 71 °C (160 °F).

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Recipes with added salt should be considered for overall sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the loaf thinly and serve cold as a snack, in sandwiches, or with vegetable salads. It can also be warmed in the oven or microwave, added to soups, or used as a filling for pies.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze – up to 3 months. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
